# Reference

## Table of Contents

### Classes

* [`glpi`](#glpi): Configures how the glpi_* resource providers reach the GLPI API.
* [`glpi::api_access`](#glpi--api_access): Bootstraps the OAuth client and service user the providers need for API v2.
* [`glpi::resources`](#glpi--resources): Declares GLPI resources from Hiera data.

### Resource types

* [`glpi_appliance`](#glpi_appliance): Manages a GLPI appliance and its member links through API v2.
* [`glpi_certificate`](#glpi_certificate): Manages a GLPI certificate and its links to computers through API v2.
* [`glpi_cluster`](#glpi_cluster): Manages a GLPI cluster (Management > Clusters) through API v2.
* [`glpi_computer_placement`](#glpi_computer_placement): Places an existing GLPI computer in an entity and a location through API v2.
* [`glpi_config`](#glpi_config): Sets an existing GLPI configuration value (Setup > General and the inventory settings) through API v2.
* [`glpi_custom_asset`](#glpi_custom_asset): Manages a GLPI custom asset (an asset of a custom asset definition) and its custom fields through API v2.
* [`glpi_domain`](#glpi_domain): Manages a GLPI domain and its links to contracts through API v2.
* [`glpi_item_placement`](#glpi_item_placement): Places an existing GLPI network device or data center in a location through API v2.
* [`glpi_location`](#glpi_location): Manages the comment of a GLPI location (dropdown) through API v2.
* [`glpi_rule`](#glpi_rule): Manages a GLPI rule (authorization, asset import or mail collector rule) through API v2.

## Classes

### <a name="glpi"></a>`glpi`

Writes a YAML file that the providers read at run time: the GLPI API v2
connection (OAuth client and service user) and the module's ownership
settings. Declare this class on the node that applies glpi_* resources.
Every glpi_* resource autorequires the file, so on the first run it exists
before any provider talks to GLPI.

#### Examples

##### 

```puppet
class { 'glpi':
  base_url      => 'https://glpi.example.com/api.php',
  client_id     => 'puppet',
  client_secret => Sensitive('...'),
  username      => 'puppet-api',
  password      => Sensitive('...'),
}
```

Data type: `Pattern[/(?i:\Ahttps?:\/\/\S+\z)/]`

GLPI API root, an http(s) URL, e.g. `https://glpi.example.com/api.php`. The
token endpoint is `<base_url>/token`, resources live under `<base_url>/v2/`.

##### <a name="-glpi--client_id"></a>`client_id`

Data type: `String[1]`

OAuth client id.

##### <a name="-glpi--client_secret"></a>`client_secret`

Data type: `Sensitive[String[1]]`

OAuth client secret.

##### <a name="-glpi--username"></a>`username`

Data type: `String[1]`

GLPI user the providers act as (password grant).

##### <a name="-glpi--password"></a>`password`

Data type: `Sensitive[String[1]]`

Password of that user.

##### <a name="-glpi--grant_type"></a>`grant_type`

Data type: `Enum['password', 'client_credentials']`

OAuth grant type.

Default value: `'password'`

##### <a name="-glpi--ssl_verify"></a>`ssl_verify`

Data type: `Boolean`

Whether to verify the GLPI TLS certificate.

Default value: `true`

##### <a name="-glpi--ssl_ca_file"></a>`ssl_ca_file`

Data type: `Optional[Stdlib::Absolutepath]`

Absolute path of the CA bundle used for verification when GLPI uses a
private CA.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-glpi--marker"></a>`marker`

Data type: `Pattern[/\S/]`

String in an object's comment that marks it as managed by Puppet. Only
marked objects are ever deleted or purged.

Default value: `'[managed by puppet]'`

##### <a name="-glpi--type_markers"></a>`type_markers`

Data type: `Hash[String[1], Pattern[/\S/]]`

Per-type marker overrides, keyed by type name, e.g.
`{ 'glpi_cluster' => '[managed by puppet: clusters]' }`.

Default value: `{}`

##### <a name="-glpi--purge_max_fraction"></a>`purge_max_fraction`

Data type: `Variant[Float[0,1], Integer[0,1]]`

Largest share of a type's marked objects one run may delete. A run that
would delete more (at least one deletion is always allowed) fails every
deletion of that type and deletes nothing. 0 and 1 may be given as
integers; the file always holds a float.

Default value: `0.5`

##### <a name="-glpi--purge_max_per_run"></a>`purge_max_per_run`

Data type: `Integer[0]`

Largest number of a type's marked objects one run may delete, whatever
the fraction allows (the smaller limit wins; per guard scope where a type
has scopes). It bounds what a run working from incomplete inputs (a
fact or data source that came back empty for part of the fleet) can
retire, which matters most when runs come often. 0: no absolute cap,
only the fraction applies.

Default value: `3`

##### <a name="-glpi--unresolved"></a>`unresolved`

Data type: `Enum['warn', 'fail']`

What a reference that matches no GLPI object does: a
`glpi_computer_placement` whose computer does not exist (or is in the
trash), a `glpi_appliance` member that matches nothing. `warn` logs a
warning and reports the resource in sync. `fail` applies everything else
the resource declares and then fails the resource with the same message,
so the run reports a failure; nothing changes on later runs while the
reference stays unresolved, but each run reports the failure again.

Default value: `'warn'`

##### <a name="-glpi--restore_trashed"></a>`restore_trashed`

Data type: `Boolean`

When a resource's object exists only in the GLPI trash and carries the
marker, bring it back (with the resource's attributes) instead of
creating a second one. An unmarked trashed object is never restored.

Default value: `false`

##### <a name="-glpi--type_restore_trashed"></a>`type_restore_trashed`

Data type: `Hash[String[1], Boolean]`

Per-type override of `restore_trashed`, keyed by type name, e.g.
`{ 'glpi_cluster' => true }`.

Default value: `{}`

##### <a name="-glpi--config_file"></a>`config_file`

Data type: `Stdlib::Absolutepath`

Absolute path of the transport file. It must be the path the agent's providers
read: `<agent confdir>/glpi_transport.yaml` (`Puppet[:confdir]` on the
node). The default is the agent's own confdir, from the `glpi_confdir`
fact; `$settings::confdir` (the COMPILING server's confdir, which differs
when server and agent use different layouts) only before that fact has
been pluginsynced.

Default value: `"${$facts['glpi_confdir'].lest || { $settings::confdir }}/glpi_transport.yaml"`

### <a name="glpi--api_access"></a>`glpi::api_access`

GLPI only issues API tokens to an OAuth client, and a token is bound to a
user. Neither can be created through the API before such a token exists, so
this class creates both locally: a PHP script boots the GLPI kernel and makes
the OAuth client, the service user (local authentication) and the user's
profile assignment match a JSON config file.

The config file (`api-bootstrap.json`) and the script
(`glpi-api-bootstrap.php`) live in `config_dir`. The class creates that
directory and owns it (owner `system_user`, mode 0700), so it must be a
directory of its own: a top-level directory (`/etc`), the GLPI install
directory and the directories GLPI itself uses (`/etc/glpi`,
`/var/lib/glpi`, `/var/log/glpi`) or anything below them are refused.
Nothing else in the directory is managed.

The script runs as `system_user` on every agent run in check mode (`unless`)
and only changes GLPI when the check reports a difference. Secrets are read
from the config file only; they never appear in a command line.

#### Examples

##### Create the client and service user used by the providers

```puppet
class { 'glpi::api_access':
  glpi_root     => '/var/www/glpi',
  client_name   => 'Puppet',
  client_id     => 'puppet',
  client_secret => Sensitive(lookup('glpi::client_secret')),
  username      => 'puppet-api',
  password      => Sensitive(lookup('glpi::api_password')),
}
```

### <a name="glpi--resources"></a>`glpi::resources`

Include this class after the main `glpi` class when you prefer data-driven
resource declarations over inline glpi_* resource blocks. Every parameter
defaults to `{}`, so including the class alone declares nothing.

A reference that must exist before the resource it is named in can be
applied is ordered when both are declared here: a nested location after its
parent, a placement after its location, a rule after its `before_rule`. The
other references (appliance members, custom asset `field_refs`) are resolved
at run time as the types describe.

#### Examples

##### Declare resources from Hiera

```puppet
include glpi::resources
```

##### Hiera data

```puppet
glpi::resources::locations:
  'Main office':
    comment: 'Head office'
  'Main office > Server room':
    comment: 'Basement'
glpi::resources::clusters:
  'Cluster A':
    cluster_type: 'Hypervisor'
glpi::resources::appliances:
  'Web shop':
    appliance_type: 'Service'
    members:
      - { itemtype: 'Computer', name: 'web1.example.com' }
glpi::resources::computer_placements:
  'web1.example.com':
    location: 'Main office > Server room'
glpi::resources::item_placements:
  'NetworkEquipment/switch1':
    location: 'Main office > Server room'
glpi::resources::configs:
  'inventory/stale_agents_delay':
    value: '14'
glpi::resources::rules:
  'Ignore lamps':
    collection: 'import_asset'
    criteria:
      - { criteria: 'name', condition: 6, pattern: '/Lamp$/' }
    actions:
      - { action_type: 'assign', field: '_ignore_import', value: '1' }
```

## Resource types

### <a name="glpi_appliance"></a>`glpi_appliance`

Appliances are matched by `name` among the appliances that are not in the
trash.

* An existing appliance of the same name without the marker is left alone:
  it is reported in sync with a warning and never changed, adopted or
  deleted.
* The marker is written first in the GLPI comment, followed by `comment`;
  `comment` reads back without it.
* `delete_properties` clears `appliance_type`, `comment` or `environment`;
  the marker stays. An unmarked appliance is not written, so nothing is
  cleared on it.
* `appliance_type` and `environment` name an appliance type and an
  appliance environment; missing ones are created. Empty means none.
* `members` are the items linked to the appliance, by itemtype and name.
  The resource is authoritative only for the itemtypes in `member_types`:
  links of other itemtypes are never read, added or removed, so links made
  by hand or by other tools coexist. Members compare as an unordered set.
* A `Computer` member matches a GLPI computer by name case-insensitively,
  or by the first DNS label of the name when the full name matches nothing
  (agents may register short names). Other members match by exact name.
  A member that matches nothing is skipped with a warning.
* `Cluster` members can be read and compared, but API v2 cannot add or
  remove a cluster link: a needed change fails the resource and must be
  made in GLPI.
* Reading the links uses the GLPI GraphQL API: the OAuth client needs the
  `graphql` scope in addition to `api` (see `glpi::api_access`).
* A new appliance is created in the root entity (id 0), recursive.
* `ensure => absent` and purge move a marked appliance to the trash. A
  trashed appliance is invisible to this type: declaring its name again
  creates a new appliance, the trashed one is not restored.

#### Examples

##### 

```puppet
glpi_appliance { 'Web shop':
  appliance_type => 'Service',
  environment    => 'Production',
  comment        => 'Shop and blog',
  member_types   => ['Computer', 'Cluster'],
  members        => [
    { 'itemtype' => 'Computer', 'name' => 'web1.example.com' },
    { 'itemtype' => 'Cluster', 'name' => 'Cluster A' },
  ],
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `glpi_appliance` type.

##### `appliance_type`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Name of the appliance type (created if missing). Empty: no type. Unset: not managed.

##### `comment`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

The comment, without the marker. Unset: the stored comment is kept.

##### `delete_properties`

Data type: `Optional[Array[Enum['appliance_type', 'comment', 'environment']]]`

Optional properties to clear on update, by attribute name. Removing an attribute from the manifest only stops Puppet managing it. The marker stays in the GLPI comment.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether the appliance should be present or absent (absent moves it to the trash).

Default value: `present`

##### `environment`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Name of the appliance environment (created if missing). Empty: none. Unset: not managed.

##### `members`

Data type: `Optional[Array[Struct[{itemtype => Enum['Computer', 'Monitor', 'NetworkEquipment', 'Peripheral', 'Phone', 'Printer', 'SoftwareLicense', 'Certificate', 'Unmanaged', 'Appliance', 'Cluster'], name => String[1]}]]]`

Items linked to the appliance. Every itemtype must be listed in `member_types`. Compared as an unordered set. Unset: links are not managed.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `glpi_appliance` type.

* [`member_types`](#-glpi_appliance--member_types)
* [`name`](#-glpi_appliance--name)

##### <a name="-glpi_appliance--member_types"></a>`member_types`

Data type: `Array[Enum['Computer', 'Monitor', 'NetworkEquipment', 'Peripheral', 'Phone', 'Printer', 'SoftwareLicense', 'Certificate', 'Unmanaged', 'Appliance', 'Cluster'], 1]`

The itemtypes this resource is authoritative for. Links of other itemtypes are ignored.

Default value: `["Computer"]`

Data type: `String[1]`

The appliance name.

### <a name="glpi_certificate"></a>`glpi_certificate`

Certificates are matched by `name` among the certificates that are not in
the trash, case-insensitively after HTML-entity decoding and Unicode
normalisation (a certificate CN in another case is the same certificate).

* An unmarked certificate of the same name is adopted: it gets the marker
  and is managed from then on (a one-time change).
* The marker is written first in the GLPI comment, followed by `comment`;
  `comment` reads back without it. Unset: the stored comment is kept.
* `dns_name`, `serial`, `expiration` and `self_signed` are written as GLPI
  stores them (`dns_name`, `serial`, `date_expiration`, `is_selfsign`).
  `expiration` is a date `YYYY-MM-DD`; an empty string clears it. Unset
  attributes are not managed.
* `delete_properties` clears `comment`, `dns_name`, `expiration` or `serial`
  of an existing certificate; the marker stays.
* `entity` is an entity's complete name (`Root entity > Customer A`) or a
  unique entity name; `entity_tag` selects the entity by its tag instead
  (mutually exclusive). Unset: not managed; a new certificate is then
  created in the default entity of the API user.
* `computers` are the computers the certificate is linked to. A computer
  matches by name case-insensitively, or by the first DNS label when the
  full name matches nothing. Only links to computers are read or written;
  links of the certificate to other item types are never touched. With
  `computers_exclusive` (default) a link to an undeclared computer is
  removed; without it, missing links are added and none is ever removed.
  A computer that matches nothing is skipped with a warning (class glpi
  `unresolved => 'warn'`) or fails the resource after the other links are
  written (`unresolved => 'fail'`). GLPI may hold the same link twice; it
  reads as one link, and an unwanted pair is removed with all its rows.
* Reading the links uses the GLPI GraphQL API: the OAuth client needs the
  `graphql` scope in addition to `api` (see `glpi::api_access`).
* `ensure => absent` and purge move a marked certificate to the trash; an
  unmarked one is never deleted. With `restore_trashed` (class glpi) a
  marked trashed certificate of the same name is restored instead of
  creating a new one.

#### Examples

##### A certificate linked to a computer

```puppet
glpi_certificate { 'www.example.com':
  dns_name    => 'www.example.com',
  serial      => '04A1B2C3',
  expiration  => '2027-02-28',
  self_signed => false,
  entity      => 'Root entity > Customer A',
  computers   => ['web1.example.com'],
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `glpi_certificate` type.

##### `comment`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

The comment, without the marker. Unset: the stored comment is kept.

##### `computers`

Data type: `Optional[Array[String[1]]]`

Names of the computers the certificate is linked to. Compared as an unordered set. Unset: links are not managed.

##### `delete_properties`

Data type: `Optional[Array[Enum['comment', 'dns_name', 'expiration', 'serial']]]`

Optional properties to clear on update, by attribute name. Removing an attribute from the manifest only stops Puppet managing it. The marker stays in the GLPI comment.

##### `dns_name`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

The DNS name. Unset: not managed.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether the certificate should be present or absent (absent moves it to the trash).

Default value: `present`

##### `entity`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Complete name or unique name of the entity. Unset: not managed.

##### `entity_tag`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Tag of the entity (alternative to `entity`), compared case-sensitively. Unset: not managed.

##### `expiration`

Data type: `Optional[Pattern[/\A(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})?\z/]]`
_*this data type contains a regex that may not be accurately reflected in generated documentation_

The expiration date, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Empty string: cleared. Unset: not managed.

##### `self_signed`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Whether the certificate is self-signed. Unset: not managed.

##### `serial`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

The serial number. Unset: not managed.

The following parameters are available in the `glpi_certificate` type.

### <a name="glpi_cluster"></a>`glpi_cluster`

Clusters are matched by `name` among the clusters that are not in the trash.

* An existing cluster of the same name without the marker is left alone: it
  is reported in sync with a warning and never changed, adopted or deleted.
* The marker is written first in the GLPI comment, followed by `comment`;
  `comment` reads back without it.
* `delete_properties` clears `cluster_type` or `comment`; the marker stays.
  An unmarked cluster is not written, so nothing is cleared on it.
* `cluster_type` names a cluster type; a missing type is created (root
  entity, recursive). An empty `cluster_type` means no type.
* A new cluster is created in the root entity (id 0). API v2 does not
  expose `is_recursive` for clusters, so GLPI's default applies.
* `ensure => absent` and purge move a marked cluster to the trash. A trashed
  cluster is invisible to this type: declaring its name again creates a new
  cluster, the trashed one is not restored.
* Cluster membership (which computers form the cluster) is not managed:
  API v2 has no endpoint for it.

#### Examples

##### 

```puppet
glpi_cluster { 'Cluster A':
  cluster_type => 'Hypervisor',
  comment      => 'Three-node cluster',
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `glpi_cluster` type.

##### `cluster_type`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Name of the cluster type (created if missing). Empty: no type. Unset: not managed.

##### `comment`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

The comment, without the marker. Unset: the stored comment is kept.

##### `delete_properties`

Data type: `Optional[Array[Enum['cluster_type', 'comment']]]`

Optional properties to clear on update, by attribute name. Removing an attribute from the manifest only stops Puppet managing it. The marker stays in the GLPI comment.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether the cluster should be present or absent (absent moves it to the trash).

Default value: `present`

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `glpi_cluster` type.

* [`name`](#-glpi_cluster--name)

##### <a name="-glpi_cluster--name"></a>`name`

namevar

Data type: `String[1]`

The cluster name.

### <a name="glpi_computer_placement"></a>`glpi_computer_placement`

An update-only type: it never creates, deletes or lists computers. A
computer that does not exist (or is in the trash) is reported with a
warning and left alone; the resource is then in sync.

* The title is the computer name. It matches a GLPI computer by name
  case-insensitively, or by the first DNS label of the name when the full
  name matches nothing (agents may register short names). Two matches fail
  the resource.
* `entity` is an entity's complete name (`Root entity > Customers > Customer A`)
  or a unique entity name. It reads back as the complete name; values are
  compared by the entity they resolve to.
* `entity_tag` selects the entity whose tag equals it (it must be unique)
  instead of `entity`; the two are mutually exclusive. Tags compare
  case-sensitively. It reads back as the tag of the computer's current
  entity.
* `location` is a location's complete name (`Main office > Branch`) or a
  unique location name; empty means no location. Compared like `entity`.
* Only the declared attributes are written, and only when they differ.
  The update goes through GLPI's normal update path: for a computer that
  an inventory agent maintains, GLPI locks the changed fields, so the next
  inventory keeps the value.
* An unknown or ambiguous entity, entity tag or location fails the resource.

#### Examples

##### 

```puppet
glpi_computer_placement { 'web1.example.com':
  entity   => 'Root entity > Customers > Customer A',
  location => 'Main office',
}
```

##### Entity by its tag

```puppet
glpi_computer_placement { 'db1.example.com':
  entity_tag => '10001',
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `glpi_computer_placement` type.

##### `entity`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Complete name or unique name of the entity. Unset: not managed.

##### `entity_tag`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Tag of the entity (alternative to `entity`), compared case-sensitively. Unset: not managed.

##### `location`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Complete name or unique name of the location. Empty: no location. Unset: not managed.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `glpi_computer_placement` type.

* [`name`](#-glpi_computer_placement--name)

##### <a name="-glpi_computer_placement--name"></a>`name`

namevar

Data type: `String[1]`

The computer name.

### <a name="glpi_config"></a>`glpi_config`

An update-only type over `/Setup/Config/<context>/<key>`: it never creates or
deletes configuration keys and never lists them (no purge).

* The title is `<context>/<key>`, for example `inventory/stale_agents_delay`
  (context `core` is the general setup, `inventory` the inventory settings).
* `value` is always a string, exactly as GLPI stores it (`'14'`, `'[2]'`, `'0'`);
  a number from the API reads back as its string.
* A key that does not exist fails the resource. The API would otherwise create
  a new, meaningless row on a write to an unknown key, so the provider reads
  the key first and refuses.
* Keys whose name suggests a secret (`pass`, `secret`, `token`, `key`, `pwd`,
  `credential`) are refused by the type, so no such value is ever read,
  compared or logged. GLPI itself hides its mail and proxy passwords from this
  API; the inventory basic-auth password is not hidden, hence the name rule.
  The rule is by name alone and also refuses harmless keys such as
  `password_min_length`.
* The value is shown in change events and in `--show_diff`-style output:
  manage only non-secret settings with this type.

#### Examples

##### 

```puppet
glpi_config { 'inventory/stale_agents_delay':
  value => '14',
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `glpi_config` type.

##### `value`

Data type: `String`

The value, as a string, as GLPI stores it.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `glpi_config` type.

* [`name`](#-glpi_config--name)

##### <a name="-glpi_config--name"></a>`name`

namevar

Data type: `String[1]`

The configuration key as `<context>/<key>`.

### <a name="glpi_custom_asset"></a>`glpi_custom_asset`

A custom asset is identified by `definition` AND `name`: the asset
definition's system name (e.g. `Website`, the `<definition>` in
`/Assets/Custom/<definition>`) and the asset name. The same name in two
definitions is two resources. Names compare case-insensitively after
HTML-entity decoding and Unicode normalisation.

* The title is `<definition>/<name>`; `definition` and `name` are taken
  from it (the name may contain `/`). A title without `/` fails, and so do
  `definition`/`name` attributes that disagree with the title.
* An unmarked asset of the same definition and name is adopted: it gets the
  marker and is managed from then on (a one-time change).
* The marker is written first in the GLPI comment, followed by `comment`;
  `comment` reads back without it. Unset: the stored comment is kept.
* `asset_type` names a value of the definition's type dropdown
  (`/Assets/Custom/<definition>Type`); a missing one is created. Empty means
  none.
* `delete_properties` clears `asset_type` or `comment` of an existing asset;
  the marker stays. A custom field is cleared by its empty string.
* `entity` is an entity's complete name (`Root entity > Customer A`) or a
  unique entity name; `entity_tag` selects the entity by its tag instead
  (mutually exclusive). Unset: not managed; a new asset is then created in
  the default entity of the API user.
* `fields` are custom fields by their system name. Only the declared keys
  are read, compared and written; other custom fields of the asset are
  never touched. An empty string clears a field. Values compare as text, so
  a dropdown field is declared by the id GLPI stores (as a string) unless it
  is listed in `field_refs`.
* `field_refs` lists the fields of `fields` whose value is the name of a GLPI
  object of the given itemtype: the name is resolved to the id on write and
  the id reads back as the name. A `Computer` matches by name
  case-insensitively, else by the first DNS label. An empty value means none.
  A name that matches nothing leaves the stored value alone with a warning
  (class glpi `unresolved => 'warn'`) or fails the resource after the rest is
  written (`unresolved => 'fail'`); 0 is never written for it.
* `ensure => absent` and purge move a marked asset to the trash; an unmarked
  one is never deleted. With `restore_trashed` (class glpi) a marked trashed
  asset of the same definition and name is restored instead of creating a new
  one. The purge guard counts per definition.

#### Examples

##### A website with custom fields

```puppet
glpi_custom_asset { 'Website/www.example.com':
  asset_type => 'Shop',
  entity     => 'Root entity > Customer A',
  comment    => 'Main site',
  fields     => {
    'url'     => 'https://www.example.com/',
    'runs_on' => 'web1.example.com',
  },
  field_refs => { 'runs_on' => 'Computer' },
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `glpi_custom_asset` type.

##### `asset_type`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Name of the value of the definition type dropdown (created if missing). Empty: no type. Unset: not managed.

##### `comment`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

The comment, without the marker. Unset: the stored comment is kept.

##### `delete_properties`

Data type: `Optional[Array[Enum['asset_type', 'comment']]]`

Optional properties to clear on update, by attribute name. Removing an attribute from the manifest only stops Puppet managing it. The marker stays in the GLPI comment.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether the asset should be present or absent (absent moves it to the trash).

Default value: `present`

##### `entity`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Complete name or unique name of the entity. Unset: not managed.

##### `entity_tag`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Tag of the entity (alternative to `entity`), compared case-sensitively. Unset: not managed.

##### `fields`

Data type: `Hash[String[1], String]`

Custom fields by system name; only these keys are managed. Empty string: cleared. Default: no field is managed.

Default value: `{}`

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `glpi_custom_asset` type.

* [`definition`](#-glpi_custom_asset--definition)
* [`field_refs`](#-glpi_custom_asset--field_refs)
* [`name`](#-glpi_custom_asset--name)

##### <a name="-glpi_custom_asset--definition"></a>`definition`

namevar

Data type: `String[1]`

System name of the custom asset definition (e.g. `Website`). Part of the identity.

##### <a name="-glpi_custom_asset--field_refs"></a>`field_refs`

Data type: `Hash[String[1], Enum['Computer', 'Appliance']]`

Fields of `fields` whose value is the name of an object of this itemtype (resolved to its id).

Default value: `{}`

##### <a name="-glpi_custom_asset--name"></a>`name`

namevar

Data type: `String[1]`

The asset name (unique within its definition).

### <a name="glpi_domain"></a>`glpi_domain`

Domains are matched by `name` among the domains that are not in the trash,
case-insensitively after HTML-entity decoding and Unicode normalisation.
The name is written as declared (Unicode included, e.g. an IDN in its
Unicode form).

* An unmarked domain of the same name is adopted: it gets the marker and
  is managed from then on (a one-time change).
* The marker is written first in the GLPI comment, followed by `comment`;
  `comment` reads back without it. Unset: the stored comment is kept.
* `expiration` is a date `YYYY-MM-DD` (GLPI reads it back with a time of
  day, which is ignored); an empty string clears it. Unset: not managed.
* `delete_properties` clears `comment` or `expiration` of an existing
  domain; the marker stays.
* `entity` / `entity_tag` select the entity by complete or unique name, or
  by tag (mutually exclusive). Unset: not managed.
* `contracts` are the contracts the domain is linked to, by name. The
  resource is authoritative only for the contracts named in
  `contract_scope` (unset: the contracts in `contracts`): a link to a
  contract outside the scope is never read, added or removed, so links
  made by hand or by other tools coexist. A declared contract outside a
  declared scope fails the resource. Moving a domain between two contracts
  of the scope links the new one and then unlinks the old one.
* A contract name that matches no live contract, or more than one, is
  skipped with a warning (class glpi `unresolved => 'warn'`) or fails the
  resource after the other links are written (`unresolved => 'fail'`).
  While any declared contract is unresolved, no contract link of the
  domain is removed at all (a typo must not strip the links that exist);
  the other links are still added.
* Reading the links uses the GLPI GraphQL API: the OAuth client needs the
  `graphql` scope in addition to `api` (see `glpi::api_access`).
* GLPI's `is_active` flag is not managed.
* `ensure => absent` and purge move a marked domain to the trash; an
  unmarked one is never deleted. With `restore_trashed` (class glpi) a
  marked trashed domain of the same name is restored instead.

#### Examples

##### A domain linked to a contract

```puppet
glpi_domain { 'example.com':
  expiration     => '2027-02-28',
  entity_tag     => '10001',
  contracts      => ['Hosting Customer A'],
  contract_scope => ['Hosting Customer A', 'Hosting Customer B'],
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `glpi_domain` type.

##### `comment`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

The comment, without the marker. Unset: the stored comment is kept.

##### `contracts`

Data type: `Optional[Array[String[1]]]`

Names of the contracts the domain is linked to (within `contract_scope`). Compared as an unordered set. Unset: links are not managed.

##### `delete_properties`

Data type: `Optional[Array[Enum['comment', 'expiration']]]`

Optional properties to clear on update, by attribute name. Removing an attribute from the manifest only stops Puppet managing it. The marker stays in the GLPI comment.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether the domain should be present or absent (absent moves it to the trash).

Default value: `present`

##### `entity`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Complete name or unique name of the entity. Unset: not managed.

##### `entity_tag`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Tag of the entity (alternative to `entity`), compared case-sensitively. Unset: not managed.

##### `expiration`

Data type: `Optional[Pattern[/\A(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})?\z/]]`
_*this data type contains a regex that may not be accurately reflected in generated documentation_

The expiration date, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Empty string: cleared. Unset: not managed.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `glpi_domain` type.

* [`contract_scope`](#-glpi_domain--contract_scope)
* [`name`](#-glpi_domain--name)

##### <a name="-glpi_domain--contract_scope"></a>`contract_scope`

Data type: `Optional[Array[String[1]]]`

Names of the contracts this resource is authoritative for. Unset: the contracts in `contracts`.

##### <a name="-glpi_domain--name"></a>`name`

namevar

Data type: `String[1]`

The domain name, kept as declared.

### <a name="glpi_item_placement"></a>`glpi_item_placement`

An update-only type: it never creates, deletes or lists items. An item
that does not exist (or is in the trash) is reported with a warning and
left alone; the resource is then in sync.

* The title is `<itemtype>/<name>`. `itemtype` is `NetworkEquipment`
  (`/Assets/NetworkEquipment`) or `DataCenter` (`/Management/DataCenter`);
  the same name under both itemtypes is two resources.
* The name matches a GLPI item of that itemtype case-insensitively and
  exactly; two live matches fail the resource.
* `location` is a location's complete name (`Main office > Branch`) or a
  unique location name; empty means no location. It reads back as the
  complete name and is compared by the location it resolves to.
* An unknown or ambiguous location fails the resource.
* The update goes through GLPI's normal update path: for an item that an
  inventory agent maintains, GLPI locks the changed field, so the next
  inventory keeps the value.

#### Examples

##### 

```puppet
glpi_item_placement { 'NetworkEquipment/switch1':
  location => 'Main office > Server room',
}
```

##### 

```puppet
glpi_item_placement { 'DataCenter/dc1':
  location => 'Main office',
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `glpi_item_placement` type.

##### `location`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Complete name or unique name of the location. Empty: no location. Unset: not managed.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `glpi_item_placement` type.

* [`itemtype`](#-glpi_item_placement--itemtype)
* [`name`](#-glpi_item_placement--name)

##### <a name="-glpi_item_placement--itemtype"></a>`itemtype`

namevar

Data type: `Enum["NetworkEquipment", "DataCenter"]`

The GLPI item type. Part of the identity.

##### <a name="-glpi_item_placement--name"></a>`name`

namevar

Data type: `String[1]`

The item name.

### <a name="glpi_location"></a>`glpi_location`

A location is identified by `name` AND `parent`: a location is matched only
among the children of `parent`, or among the top-level locations when no
parent is declared. The same name under another parent is a different
location, but two same-name locations under different parents cannot be
declared in one catalog (the rebuilt resource is titled by name alone, so
they collide as a duplicate declaration). A missing location is created,
never moved.

* `parent` is the parent's complete name: a top-level location by its name,
  a nested one as `Grandparent > Parent`; empty means top level.
* The title is the plain name of a top-level location, or `Parent > Name` for
  a nested one (`parent` and `name` are then taken from the title). A name
  must not contain ` > `.
* This is a match-and-update type: an existing location keeps everything the
  resource does not declare, is never marked and is never deleted.
  `ensure => absent` only logs a warning. Locations are not purged.
* Only `comment` is ever changed on an existing location. Removing `comment`
  from the manifest keeps the stored comment.
* `delete_properties => ['comment']` empties the stored comment.
* A new location is created in the root entity (id 0), recursive.
* Names and comments are compared after HTML-entity decoding and Unicode
  normalisation.

#### Examples

##### Location with a description

```puppet
glpi_location { 'Main office':
  comment => 'Head office',
}
```

##### Location below another one

```puppet
glpi_location { 'Main office > North branch':
  comment => 'Branch office',
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `glpi_location` type.

##### `comment`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

The location comment.

##### `delete_properties`

Data type: `Optional[Array[Enum['comment']]]`

Optional properties to clear on update, by attribute name. Removing an attribute from the manifest only stops Puppet managing it.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether the location should exist. `absent` is a warning and changes nothing.

Default value: `present`

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `glpi_location` type.

* [`name`](#-glpi_location--name)
* [`parent`](#-glpi_location--parent)

##### <a name="-glpi_location--name"></a>`name`

namevar

Data type: `String[1]`

The location name (unique among the children of one parent).

##### <a name="-glpi_location--parent"></a>`parent`

namevar

Data type: `String`

Complete name of the parent location (`A` or `A > B`). Empty (default): top level. Part of the identity.

Default value: `''`

### <a name="glpi_rule"></a>`glpi_rule`

Rules are matched by `name` across the supported collections, so a name must
be unique among the `right`, `import_asset` and `mail_collector` rules.

* An existing rule of the same name without the marker is adopted: it keeps
  its comment, gains the marker and is brought to the declared state. Unmarked
  rules of other names are never touched; purge sees only marked rules.
* `criteria` and `actions` compare as unordered sets. When they differ, all
  criteria (or actions) of the rule are replaced.
* An action whose `field` is `profiles_id` or `entities_id` may name the
  profile or entity (entity name or complete name) instead of its id.
* A new rule is created in the root entity (id 0), recursive, with
  condition 0; an adopted rule keeps its entity.

#### Examples

##### Authorization rule from an LDAP group

```puppet
glpi_rule { 'Staff rule':
  collection => 'right',
  criteria   => [{ 'criteria' => 'memberof', 'condition' => 2, 'pattern' => 'example-group' }],
  actions    => [
    { 'action_type' => 'assign', 'field' => 'profiles_id', 'value' => 'Technician' },
    { 'action_type' => 'assign', 'field' => 'is_recursive', 'value' => '1' },
  ],
}
```

##### Asset import rule ranked above another rule

```puppet
glpi_rule { 'Ignore lamps':
  collection  => 'import_asset',
  criteria    => [
    { 'criteria' => 'itemtype', 'condition' => 0, 'pattern' => 'Peripheral' },
    { 'criteria' => 'name', 'condition' => 6, 'pattern' => '/Lamp$/' },
  ],
  actions     => [{ 'action_type' => 'assign', 'field' => '_ignore_import', 'value' => '1' }],
  before_rule => 'Device update (by serial)',
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `glpi_rule` type.

##### `actions`

Data type: `Array[Struct[{action_type => String[1], field => String[1], value => String}]]`

The rule actions. For the fields `profiles_id` and `entities_id`, `value` may be a profile or entity name; it is read back as the name. Compared as an unordered set.

##### `before_rule`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Name of a rule in the same collection this rule must rank above. In sync while this rule ranks above it; otherwise the rule is moved directly above it. (Named `before_rule` because `before` is a Puppet metaparameter.)

##### `collection`

Data type: `Enum['right', 'import_asset', 'mail_collector']`

The rule collection: authorizations (`right`), asset import (`import_asset`) or mail collector (`mail_collector`). A rule cannot move between collections.

##### `criteria`

Data type: `Array[Struct[{criteria => String[1], condition => Integer, pattern => String}]]`

The rule criteria. `condition` is a GLPI condition code, listed by `/Rule/Collection/<collection>/CriteriaCondition` (0 is, 2 contains, 6 regular expression matches, ...). Compared as an unordered set.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether the rule should be present or absent.

Default value: `present`

##### `is_active`

Data type: `Boolean`

Whether the rule is active.

Default value: `true`

##### `match`

Data type: `Enum['AND', 'OR']`

How the criteria combine.

Default value: `AND`

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `glpi_rule` type.

* [`name`](#-glpi_rule--name)

##### <a name="-glpi_rule--name"></a>`name`

namevar

Data type: `String[1]`

The rule name (unique among the supported collections).
